question: How do you use EXPLAIN ANALYZE and choose the right index type in PostgreSQL?
title: PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE and Indexing
direct_answer: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query and shows actual timings, row counts, and operation types. Look for Seq Scan on large tables (needs an index), high actual rows vs estimate mismatch (stale statistics — run ANALYZE), and slow Sort or Hash operations. B-tree indexes cover equality and range queries (the default). GIN indexes for JSONB, array membership, full-text search. GiST for geometric types and range exclusion. Hash indexes for equality-only workloads. Partial indexes for filtered subsets.
interviewer_intent: Tests production database optimization knowledge — EXPLAIN ANALYZE is the key diagnostic tool.

sections.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE and indexing
sections.content:
-- EXPLAIN ANALYZE — run in psql or via SQLAlchemy
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON)
SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'test@example.com';

-- Output tells you:
-- Seq Scan: reading all rows (no useful index)
-- Index Scan: using an index
-- Bitmap Heap Scan: reading pages from index hint
-- Actual Rows vs Plan Rows: large mismatch = stale stats → run ANALYZE

-- B-tree (default) — equality, range, ORDER BY
CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created ON orders(created_at DESC);

-- Partial index — only index active users
CREATE INDEX idx_active_users ON users(email) WHERE is_active = true;

-- Composite index — multiple columns
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_status ON orders(user_id, status, created_at);
-- Column order matters: user_id must be in WHERE for this to help

-- GIN for JSONB
CREATE INDEX idx_product_metadata ON products USING GIN(metadata);

-- SQLAlchemy index definitions
from sqlalchemy import Index
Index('ix_users_email', User.email)  # B-tree
Index('ix_product_metadata', Product.metadata, postgresql_using='gin')

seo.metaTitle: PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE and Index Types — B-tree, GIN, Partial
seo.metaDescription: PostgreSQL performance: EXPLAIN ANALYZE output interpretation, B-tree vs GIN indexes, partial indexes, composite index column order.

speakable_v2.hook: EXPLAIN ANALYZE is the X-ray of your query — Seq Scan on a large table means a missing index, high row estimate mismatch means stale statistics.

beats.content: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query. Look for Seq Scan on large tables (add an index), Node Loops × cost, and actual rows vs estimated rows (big mismatch → run ANALYZE to refresh statistics).
B-tree is the default — covers equality, range, and ORDER BY. GIN for JSONB and arrays. Partial index WHERE is_active = true covers only the rows you actually query — smaller, faster.

Composite index column order matters: the first column must be in your WHERE clause or the index won't be used. CREATE INDEX ... ON orders(user_id, status) helps WHERE user_id = X queries, not WHERE status = Y alone.

speakable_v2.cap: Every index slows down writes. Check pg_stat_user_indexes for unused indexes — idx_scan = 0 after weeks of production traffic means the index is waste.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with connection pooling with PgBouncer, or VACUUM and autovacuum behavior for table bloat.
